content.overview: Article 114 provides that after the House of the People has granted demands under Article 113, an Appropriation Bill is introduced to provide for appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of India of all moneys required to meet the grants and the charged expenditure. No amendment may be proposed in either House which would vary the amount or alter the destination of any grant or vary the amount of charged expenditure. Subject to the Constitution, no money may be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law.
content.glance: After grants: Appropriation Bill for grants + charged expenditure. No amendment varying amount/destination of grant or charged amount. No withdrawal without appropriation law.
content.study:
Article 114:
(1) As soon as may be after the grants under Article 113 have been made by the House of the People, a Bill is introduced to provide for appropriation out of the Consolidated Fund of India of all moneys required to meet—
(a) the grants so made by the House of the People; and
(b) the expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India but not exceeding the amount shown in the statement previously laid before Parliament.

(2) No amendment shall be proposed to any such Bill in either House which will have the effect of varying the amount or altering the destination of any grant or of varying the amount of any expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund.

(3) Subject to the provisions of Articles 115 and 116, no money shall be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India except under appropriation made by law passed in accordance with the provisions of this article.

Examination: Appropriation Bill content; restriction on amendments; constitutional bar on withdrawal without appropriation.

sections.heading: Appropriation process
sections.body:
1. After LS grants under Art 113, Appropriation Bill introduced.
2. Covers grants + charged expenditure (within previously shown amounts).
3. No amendment varying grant amount/destination or charged amount.
4. No withdrawal from Consolidated Fund except under appropriation law (subject to Arts 115–116).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain Appropriation Bills under Article 114.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 114, after the House of the People has made grants under Article 113, an Appropriation Bill is introduced to appropriate from the Consolidated Fund of India the moneys required for those grants and for charged expenditure. No amendment may vary the amount or destination of any grant or the amount of charged expenditure. Subject to Articles 115 and 116, no money may be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund except under appropriation made by law under this article.

examTips: Appropriation Bill after grants; restricted amendments; no withdrawal without law.

keyTakeaways: Art 114: Appropriation Bill; restricted amendments; appropriation required for withdrawal.
